value.rationale: The original spiking map is used as a state-update model, so global one-step invertibility determines whether backward states can be reconstructed uniquely from measurements. The sharp all-parameter diagram identifies three qualitatively distinct inverse geometries, a counterintuitive large-step restoration of invertibility for \(\alpha<10/17\), and a critical map smooth at every finite point but not uniformly invertible at infinity. Beyond the boundary it proves persistent three-or-more inverse branches, not merely an arbitrary isolated numerical coincidence. The degree-one odd-fiber law covers all regular targets. These exact structural distinctions are absent from the inspected forward-bifurcation studies and cannot be reduced to a trivial substitution or finite numerical exercise.
